current.title: Foskaay GGI - core, SDK, game demo, cost ladder, storage + event-based Foskaay GGI Midchain + Ludo demo on the Foskaay GGI Midchain (on-chain rules, free moves) + v7 single-core midchain (event-only, $1/1000 target) + moved to its own repo (foskaay-ggi)

items.t: (1) Foskaay GGI CORE - 4 unopinionated contracts (the rail)
(1i) SessionRegistry DONE - open/close sessions, participant authorities, session keys scope+expiry, 1..N participants, un-front-runnable ids, capped TTL; 35/35 tests
(1ii) SessionState DONE - signed events with strictly-increasing sequence (no replay/reorder), opaque payloads, off-chain digest commit + final seal, bounded storage; 28/28 tests
(1iii) Session keys - silent signer + on-chain scope/expiry token, so players never see a popup
(1iv) Randomness - commit-reveal seed(s), stored as a LIST for future extra streams; hash(seed, counter)
(1v) FeeVault - per-session fee on open and settle; destination = owner wallet; charged on devnet too
(1vi) Foundry tests for each core contract (local, no chain, no cost)
(1vii) Live Arc testnet proof: one real session opened, acted on, settled, and verified on-chain

(1viii) RENAME DONE - GlobalFolkGames Gasless Infrastructure -> Foskaay Gasless Games Infrastructure (short: Foskaay GGI). Folder foskaay-ggi/, URL /foskaay-ggi/demos/, npm @foskaay/ggi-*. arcv2m17 (GFG-BS) left untouched. 4 core contracts redeployed to Arc testnet; live proof PASS.
(2) Foskaay GGI SDK - the one-line integration
(2i) @foskaay/ggi-contracts-sdk - Solidity interfaces + deployed addresses per network
(2ii) @foskaay/ggi-sdk - open/act/dispute/settle wrappers + session-key signing + read helpers
(2iii) A README a stranger can follow: install, adapter, four calls, measured cost
(3) FIRST DEMO - prove Foskaay GGI works for a real game
(3i) Choose the first demo genre (owner pick: idle or casual). Decide before building.
(3ii) Build the demo 50-line adapter (the only game-specific code)
(3iii) Wire the demo to the SDK and prove it plays gasless end to end
(3iv) Ship the demo live and playable from /foskaay-ggi/demos/ on a phone
(3v) Ported MagicBlock on-chain Generals to Arc as the first real demo: GeneralsGame.sol keeps the board and rules on-chain, every move gated by canSign; 138/138 forge tests
(3vi) GeneralsGame deployed to Arc testnet 0xD674eD1f118855868b4B002F4A167C953Cc549ca; playable PvP page at /foskaay-ggi/demos/pvp/generals/ with MagicBlock graphics, moves relayed by the sponsor

(3vii) Agent findings recorded: the missing Foskaay GGI Midchain + the EVM tools Arc inherits we had not used (eth_call free execution, EIP-712, hash chain, EIP-7702, EIP-1153); written into the v5 build guide, the Research library (ggi-Foskaay GGI Midchain), and arcv2m18

(3viii) Foskaay GGI Midchain prototype built and proven on Arc testnet: GeneralsMidchain pure rules engine + EIP-712 signed hash-chained moves via eth_call, verifier replay PASS; no core change (4 core + 1 optional stands)
(3ix) PvP demo card links to the live page and carries a plain-language note on what is gasless and how cost works
(4) Cost proof (the number that sells Foskaay GGI)
(4i) Measure the real per-session sponsor cost on Arc and publish it vs MagicBlock ER
(4ii) Prove the floor: heavy play costs the same as light play inside a session
(4iii) Live measured cost per match on Arc testnet, unbatched vs batched, recorded in foskaay-ggi/deployments/generals-cost.json

(4iv) Foskaay GGI Midchain cost measured on Arc testnet: port 0.098172/match (about 10 games/1 USD), Foskaay GGI Midchain unbatched 0.012206 (about 81), batched 0.009788 (about 102); recorded in foskaay-ggi/deployments/midchain-cost*.json
(5) OPTIONAL patterns - offered, never enforced (build only when a game asks)
(5i) Batched Settlement - Merkle window flush, cadence chosen by the dev (never forced to 100/1h)
(5ii) Managed Accounts - PlayerCore-style single account per player with slots (a cost optimisation)
(5iii) Verifiers - per-game referee for disputes (Ludo first, when it matters)
(5iv) Session reader/explorer - so sessions and receipts are visible (MagicBlock needed one too)

(5v) Event-only handover/settle in core (no SSTORE on the happy path, events for eth_getLogs) so the Foskaay GGI Midchain can approach the v5 target of about 1000 games/1 USD; the remaining cost is core storage writes, not moves

(5vi) Event-only handover/settle prototype tested on Arc testnet: EventOnlyCore emits logs (no SSTORE) and verifies player signatures; 0.001709 USDC/match = about 585 games/1 USD (vs 81 for the core Foskaay GGI Midchain, 10 for the board port); 4 tests pass

(5vii) Event-based Foskaay GGI Midchain batched test done on Arc testnet: handoverMany/settleMany put many games in one tx; per game 0.001098 (3), 0.000939 (5), 0.000820 (10), 0.000713 (100) USDC = about 910/1064/1219/1403 games per 1 USD; crosses the v5 $1/1000 target at 5 games per batch; link is inside the Handover event so 2 txs not 3

(5viii) PENDING owner decision: build the event-based Foskaay GGI Midchain into CORE (UUPS logic upgrade, same address, append-only, + nullifier) and SDKs (handover/settle/signMove/verifyMidchain); batching stays optional; needs architecture.json update first

(5vii) PENDING owner decision: test the BATCHED event-only variant (many sessions per tx) to reach the v5 target of about 1000 games/1 USD, then decide what event-only capability (if any) goes into core + SDKs (needs replay protection/nullifier)
(6) GFG itself migrates onto Foskaay GGI (later - after GI is proven)
(6i) Decide how GFG maximises GI (owner call: account layout, cadence, patterns)
(6ii) Ludo becomes the first real GFG game on GI
(6iii) Then points, lives, premium as event/slot types
(6iv) Then multiplayer, competitions, AGM, ERC-20 rewards
(6v) Retire the old GFG settlement path (arcv2m17) once GI carries everything
(7) Ludo demo on the Foskaay GGI Midchain (Arc): on-chain rules, free moves, gasless
(7i) Port the real ludo-lab mechanics into the demo contracts (two dice, double-six bonus, capture "pe", 45s timer, position scoring 4P 100/50/25/0, 2P 100/0)
(7ii) Relay is stateless: rolls, moves, passes and board reads are FREE; only connect + settle are transactions
(7iii) Contract is the ONLY rules engine: added previewLog view, relay replays the move log through the contract (no server truth, no localStorage)
(7iv) Tests 34/34 including previewLog == settle parity and tamper rejection
(7v) Upgraded the demo contracts IN PLACE (previewLog added): addresses unchanged, data preserved, cost printed
(7vi) Frontend: ludo-lab board + 3D dice skin driven by the contract board (no localStorage)
(7vii) Live proof on Arc testnet: 2 transactions (connect 0.0125 + settle 0.0119 USDC), 119 free midchain calls, tampered log rejected
(7viii) Owner tests the demo on a real phone

(7ix) v7 core: SINGLE SessionRegistry (FeeVault merged in, direct transfer to destination, fee 0.0004 unbatched / 0.0002 batched, one SSTORE = paid flag + seed/participant commitment), UUPS/OZ; 22/22 tests
(7x) Pure Ludo game (FoskaayGGILudo): getInitialState/applyMove/isTerminal, board as bytes, points INSIDE the midchain state, no per-move SSTORE, capture "pe" matches ludo-lab; tests
(7xi) Deployed to Arc testnet: core 0x9f078527082b3bCc7c00e27f7C53D31CF1D17A85, Ludo 0xc3Dd1243B74373Bc015Fd305727E729785B41C08 (0.0717 USDC)
(7xii) Midchain relay: every move is a free eth_call + signed hash chain; only handover + settle are txs; NO replay. Live: 2 txs, ~0.0035 USDC/match, ~280 games/$1 on testnet (25 Gwei)
(7xiii) Ludo page: tx ids link to the Arc explorer, Foskaay GGI Explorer link, blinking tokens + centre dice, crown only after a real finish, token move
(7xiv) Explorer: single core + Midchain tab (hash-chain verify to the on-chain final hash)
(7xv) Owner creates + approves the PR
(7xvi) Swap remote to the new standalone repo github.com/SolomonFoskaay/foskaay-ggi (branch osv1Arc kept) and push for the first PR
(7xvii) Owner tests the live Ludo demo on the PR (meter, Foskaay GGI Explorer, Arc explorer links)
